newsitem.title: UK: S&P cuts Kellogg senior unsecured debt rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts Kellogg senior unsecured debt rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it lowered its senior unsecured debt and corporate credit ratings on Kellogg Co. to AA from AAA.
In addition, the rating on Kellogg's Rule 415 shelf registration has also been lowered to preliminary AA from preliminary AAA
"These ratings have been removed from CreditWatch where they were placed Nov. 18, 1996," S&P said in a statement.
S&P also affirmed the A1 plus commercial paper rating which was not on CreditWatch.
"The ratings outlook is stable," it said, adding that about $1.8 billion of total debt is outstanding.

The agency said the downgrade reflected increased business risk in the U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market, which accounts for about a third of Kellogg's total volume, Kellogg's increase use of debt financing, and the company's continued focus on aggressive share repurchases.
The previous AAA rating was based on Kellogg's capital structure and the stable domestic cereal category, it said.
It said these factors had resulted in very predictable cash flow and earnings growth for Kellogg.

S&P noted that the industry wide price reductions of 1996 had a negative impact on all the major industry players, but Kellogg has also experienced lower volumes since the pricing actions were implemented.

It said this was uncharacteristic for the market leader. S&P said it believed the pricing environment remained uncertain and the 1996 pricing activity indicated a permanent increase in business risk in the domestic ready-to-eat cereal market.

S&P said the recently completed $455 million debt financed Lender's acquisition, combined with significant debt financed share repurchases during 1996 have caused total debt to almost double from year end 1995 levels and credit protection measures to erode significantly.

"The increase in debt also signals Kellogg's less conservative financial policy," the agency said. "Kellogg's ratings reflect the company's strong market and financial positions despite the negative impact of the increased price competition in the domestic cereal market."

S&P said the rating benefits from global diversification, and favourable global growth prospects which are expected to partially mitigate the uncertainty in the U.S. cereal market and the company's relatively narrow business profile.

"The outlook anticipates that Kellogg will maintain its strong market position and financial profile. The ratings include flexibility for continued share repurchases and acquisition activity," S&P said.
